column1: # Every *direct* dependency of this crate must appear here with a purpose
# and a safety/security relevance note. `src/compliance/soup.rs` merges
# these annotations with the real dependency graph from Cargo.lock to
# produce the CycloneDX SBOM at GET /api/compliance/sbom, and its unit
# tests fail the build when a direct dependency is missing (or when an
# entry names a package that is no longer depended on).
# Transitive dependencies are listed in the SBOM but are NOT individually
# annotated. Stating that boundary is more honest than implying we have
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.

column2: Web application framework: boot, routing, config, background workers, model error types.
column3: Safety-relevant. Owns request routing and the middleware stack, so a defect could bypass the auth/ABAC guard. Widely used, actively maintained; pinned by Cargo.lock.

column2: Serialization framework for every wire type and the stored JSONB payload.
column3: Safety-relevant. A mis-serialized payload could corrupt a stored pathway or an audit snapshot. De facto Rust standard; extremely widely exercised.

column2: JSON encoding/decoding, and the canonical form the audit hash chain digests.
column3: Safety-relevant. Key ordering (BTreeMap, preserve_order disabled) is load-bearing for chain verification across a JSONB round-trip.

column2: Async runtime.
column3: Safety-relevant. Runtime failure means service unavailability, not data corruption. Industry standard.

column2: Async methods in traits (loco Hooks, SeaORM migrations).
column3: Not safety-relevant. Compile-time macro only, no runtime behaviour of its own.

column2: HTTP server, extractors, and response types underneath loco.
column3: Safety-relevant. Header and path extraction feed the auth guard and the purpose-of-use audit context.

column2: Structured logging and spans.
column3: Security-relevant. The no-secrets-in-logs invariant is enforced at call sites, not by this crate.

column2: Log formatting, filtering, and the JSON layer.
column3: Security-relevant. Misconfiguration could emit more detail than intended; log level is deployment-controlled.

column2: Pattern matching in payload validation.
column3: Safety-relevant. Used only on length-capped input (validation::MAX_TEXT_LEN), which bounds the catastrophic-backtracking risk.

column2: This crate's own sea-orm-migration migrator (path dependency).
column3: Safety-relevant. Owns the schema, including the audit_logs compliance columns. First-party code, not third-party SOUP.

column2: Async ORM and query builder over PostgreSQL.
column3: Safety-relevant. All persistence, including the audit trail and the redaction sweep, goes through it. Query construction uses its typed builders, not string concatenation.

column2: Timestamps, durations, and the microsecond truncation the audit chain depends on.
column3: Safety-relevant. Chain digests bind created_at as epoch microseconds; a precision change would break verification.

column2: Declarative validation attributes.
column3: Not safety-relevant today: the substantive rules live in src/validation.rs, which does not use it.

column2: Public record identifiers (pid) and audit/export job ids.
column3: Safety-relevant. v4 generation uses the OS RNG; a weak id would make records guessable.

column2: Embeds static assets (Swagger UI) into the binary.
column3: Not safety-relevant. Serves documentation assets only; no clinical data path.

column2: Global allocator for MUSL static builds.
column3: Safety-relevant. An allocator defect would be a process-wide fault. Enabled only for the musl target.

column2: Metrics registry and text-exposition rendering for /metrics.prom.
column3: Not safety-relevant. Counters only; the endpoint exposes no record data.

column2: SHA-256 for the tamper-evident audit hash chain.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The integrity evidence for HIPAA §164.312(c) rests entirely on this implementation. RustCrypto, widely audited, constant-time not required for a hash.

column2: Canonical matching engine; its CarePathway type is also this service's API DTO (path dependency).
column3: Safety-relevant. A false match can conflate two distinct pathways. First-party code with its own spec, property tests, and no-IO posture.

column2: Offline PASETO v4.public verification and the shared ABAC policy engine (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Every authentication and authorization decision depends on it. First-party code with its own forgery and policy-property test suites.

column2: Serialises tests that mutate process-wide environment variables.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Parameterised test cases.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Snapshot assertions.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Mints throwaway Ed25519 keys so the token-verification path is tested in-process.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact; the test seed is not a secret.

column2: Mints PASETO v4.public tokens in the auth unit tests.
column3: Test-only in this crate. The production verification path lives in authentication-verifier.

column2: Encodes test key material into the JWK-shaped key set.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: The `TestServer` loco's testing harness hands to a request test; used by the compliance request tests.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Temporary directories for the artifact-store tests (SEC-B4 path-confinement pins).
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Loads AWS/S3-compatible credentials and region from the standard chain, for the optional S3 artifact backend.
column3: Optional (`s3` feature); absent from a default build. Sources credentials only — it never holds a secret this crate mints. Deployments using the local filesystem backend do not compile it.

column2: S3-compatible object storage for bulk export artifacts, including presigned short-lived download URLs.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT and optional (`s3` feature). Chosen over hand-rolled SigV4 precisely because request signing cannot be verified in this repository's test environment without a live endpoint or the published AWS vectors; an unverified signing implementation that looks finished is the worse risk. Handles clinical export artifacts, so its correctness bounds who can read a bulk export.

column2: Credential value types shared by aws-config and aws-sdk-s3.
column3: Optional (`s3` feature). Type definitions only; pulled in explicitly so the credential surface is named in this register rather than arriving as an invisible transitive.

column2: Second integrity digest alongside SHA-256 for the audit chain and record hashes.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Part of the tamper-evidence for HIPAA §164.312(c). Kept for structural diversity: SHA-3 is a sponge construction, unrelated to SHA-256's Merkle-Damgard chaining, so a cryptanalytic advance against one design family does not transfer. Also FIPS 202, so it carries NIST standing while being structurally independent of SHA-2. RustCrypto, same maintainers as the sha2 crate already registered here.

column2: Keyed integrity MACs (HMAC-SHA256) with HKDF domain separation, key sourcing, zeroization, and key generation (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The MAC is the only stored integrity value an adversary holding just the database cannot forge — the SHA-256 and SHA-3 digests are unkeyed with published pre-image formats. Extracted into one shared crate rather than copied per service precisely because a key-handling defect in a copy would not announce itself: it would make MACs forgeable while every test stayed green. First-party code with its own test suite, including golden vectors cross-checked against an independent HKDF implementation.

column2: Embedded full-text search index over care-pathway records (src/search/): the name/condition-code/intervention search surface and the duplicate detector's candidate blocking.
column3: Indirect. It never decides clinical content: the database is the source of truth and every hit is resolved against it, so a stale or wrong index degrades retrieval (a pathway a search fails to surface) rather than corrupting a record. A missed hit can still mean a duplicate pathway is created, which is why the index is rebuildable (`cargo loco task search_reindex`) and rebuilt automatically when empty.

column2: Real-broker durable-bus relay sink (BUS-3, src/relay.rs FluvioSink). Optional, behind this crate's own `fluvio` Cargo feature (off by default) — a default build carries none of it.
column3: Security-relevant when the feature is enabled. Ships the canonical event envelope (which can carry care-pathway-linked clinical data, including condition codes and interventions) to an external broker over the network; the relay never sends an entity's committed change without its outbox row, but a defect here could misroute or drop events reaching downstream consumers. Not present in a default release artefact.

column2: Statistical benchmarking harness for the request-path micro-benchmarks in benches/.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.
